children: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, net interest income rose 19.6% year over year to $1.0B. Total loans were $185.0B, up 4.0% from December 31, 2025.
Nine-month net interest income: $1.0B, up 19.6% YoY
Higher interest income is the primary earnings driver disclosed; the release attributes growth partly to funding actions and asset-pool volume.
Growth was partly tied to a larger FCSIC insurance distribution, a factor that may not recur at the same level.
Loan growth expands the balance sheet; the release links it primarily to asset-pool purchases.
Capital increased, and AgriBank said it exceeded all regulatory minimums, including additional buffers.
Liquidity coverage: 153 days; regulator minimum 90 days
Coverage was above the stated regulatory minimum, supporting capacity to meet maturing debt obligations.

This is a third-quarter financial update, with nine-month results showing higher net interest income and loan growth. The next catalyst would be full-year results showing whether earnings growth persists and whether credit quality remains stable amid agricultural market volatility.
